newsitem.title: USA: Allegiance generates $137 mln cash flow.
newsitem.headline: Allegiance generates $137 mln cash flow.

text.p: Allegiance Corp, which provides products and cost-managment services to the health care industry, said Friday it generated $137 million of free cash flow in the first half of 1997.
This, in part, enabled it to retire $173.8 million of long-term debt in 1997, ending the second quarter with $936.6 million.

Allegiance, which became an independent public company last fall, reported that second-quarter sales, as anticipated, were down 1.4 percent to $1.075 billion from pro forma sales of $1.090 billion a year ago.
The decline reflected the company's efforts to reduce sales of less-profitable products and services, it said.
"Sales of the company's self-manufactured surgical products and cost-management services increased in the quarter, an indication of early success of the company's sales programs," Allegiance said.
The company earned $22 million on the quarter ended June 30, compared to pro forma net income of $11.8 million in the same period a year ago.
"Contributing to the rise in earnings were lower administrative and interest expenses, combined with a reduction in goodwill amortization," the company said.
